title: Ulyana and the Sigil
premise: Xanthe Galloway, a mercenary bound by covenant to the goddess Ulyana—who fell silent ten years ago when magic was outlawed—survives by selling hollow charms in the gray city of Vask. When prayers across the realm suddenly begin to be answered again, Xanthe discovers the old gods are waking, but something is answering in their place: a hungry counterfeit wearing Ulyana's sigil. To reforge the broken covenant between mortal and divine realms, Xanthe must gather the scattered shards of Ulyana's true name, confront the impostor god feeding on stolen faith, and choose between the loyalty that sustained him for a decade and the truth that she abandoned her faithful deliberately. In the end, Xanthe sacrifices his own covenant-mark to complete the reforging, becoming the bridge between realms himself—and Ulyana, restored, offers him not servitude but partnership.
about_author: W. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloging medieval charm-books and votive inscriptions before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about faith, bureaucracy of the divine, and people who keep promises long after it stops making sense.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Vigil
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Ten years after the Silence, Xanthe sells inert charms in outlawed-magic Vask, hiding his still-warm covenant mark beneath a glove. A child's prayer he overhears goes unanswered, and he quietly performs a small forbidden rite himself. Emotional beat: weary devotion—the ache of serving a god who no longer speaks.

chapters.title: Smoke Over the Wardmarket
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The city's anti-magic enforcers raid the wardmarket; Xanthe's friend and fence, Odile, is arrested for possessing a relic. During the chaos, every candle in the district flares at once—the first sign the gods are answering again. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into wonder, and guilt over Odile's capture.

chapters.title: What Answered
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A desperate widow thanks Xanthe for a prayer 'Ulyana' answered—but the healing left a sigil burned into her skin that Xanthe doesn't recognize. He compares it to his own mark: similar, wrong. Something is answering prayers in Ulyana's name. Emotional beat: dawning dread beneath relief.

chapters.title: The Marked Woman
chapters.summary: POV Sera, an inquisitor's clerk secretly marked by the false god, ordered to hunt others who bear sigils—including the charm-seller witnesses describe. She tracks Xanthe but hesitates when she sees his grief at Odile's sentencing. Emotional beat: divided loyalty, the first crack in her certainty.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, flashback-heavy. We learn how Ulyana went silent mid-battle, how Xanthe kept the covenant anyway, and what the final words were: 'If I do not answer, do not look for me.' He decides to break that instruction. Emotional beat: love curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Undercroft of Names
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe and Sera, uneasy allies. Following archival clues, they breach a sealed undercroft where pre-Outlawing priests stored fragments of divine names on lead tablets. One shard hums at Xanthe's touch: a piece of Ulyana's true name. Emotional beat: awe and trespass, the thrill of recovered truth.

chapters.title: Sermons in Ash
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The false god's cult grows openly; its preacher heals crowds and demands total surrender. Sera attends undercover and feels the pull of belonging she never found in the inquisition. Her mark warms approvingly. Emotional beat: seduction of certainty, temptation to stop asking questions.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe bargains with a corrupt magistrate to free Odile, paying with his last true charm—and learning the magistrate already serves the new god. Odile, freed, warns him: the shards are bait. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against prudence; the cost of old friendships.

chapters.title: The Second Shard
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In a drowned chapel, Xanthe retrieves a second shard guarded by a revenant priest who mistakes him for Ulyana's herald. The shard shows him a vision: Ulyana going silent deliberately, sealing something out. Emotional beat: revelation as wound—his goddess chose silence.

chapters.title: Heresy of the Heart
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Sera's inquisitor superior discovers her mark and gives her a choice: burn it off and be promoted, or be purged alongside the cultists. She burns nothing and runs, taking the inquisition's map of all known sigil-bearers. Emotional beat: identity chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Court
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe infiltrates the false god's cathedral and sees it plainly: a thing of stitched divinity wearing Ulyana's sigil, grown fat on answered prayers. It recognizes him and offers him Ulyana's voice back—recorded, replayed, a puppet-god. Emotional beat: horror and a terrible homesickness.

chapters.title: Do Not Look For Me
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Shattered by the vision of Ulyana's deliberate silence, Xanthe nearly surrenders his shards to the counterfeit. Sera talks him back from the edge, arguing that truth—even painful truth—is worth more than comfortable lies. Emotional beat: rock bottom, then the choice to continue.

chapters.title: The Third Shard and the Traitor's Road
chapters.summary: POV alternating Xanthe/Sera. Journey into the borderlands where the veil between realms is thin; they retrieve a third shard from a shrine tended by a hermit who once was Ulyana's high priest—and who reveals the counterfeit escaped through the seal Ulyana made. Emotional beat: companionship forged on the road.

chapters.title: What the Seal Was For
chapters.summary: POV Sera. At the hermit's fire, the full history emerges: the gods grew predatory; Ulyana sealed the veil to starve them, accepting silence as the price, trusting her faithful to endure without miracles. The counterfeit is what slipped through before the seal closed. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into understanding.

chapters.title: Vask Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Returning to Vask, they find the city half-converted, the inquisition co-opted, Odile organizing a quiet resistance of marked and unmarked alike. Xanthe must decide whether to use civilians as cover for the final ritual. Emotional beat: leadership's burden; refusing to spend people like coin.

chapters.title: The Fourth Shard Is a Person
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The final shard isn't lead—it's the widow from chapter three, whose healed body carries a living fragment of Ulyana's name. The counterfeit's cult comes for her; Sera holds the tenement stair alone. Emotional beat: courage without magic; ordinary people as the vessel of the sacred.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In the ruined undercroft, Xanthe begins the covenant-reforging ritual, joining four shards to his own mark. The counterfeit arrives early, tearing through Vask's wards to claim the assembled name. Emotional beat: terrible momentum, everything staked on one act.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Name
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Climax. The counterfeit and the reawakening Ulyana contend through Xanthe's body, each claiming the name he holds. He realizes the covenant was always meant to be spoken jointly by god and faithful—he speaks Ulyana's name back to her, completing it. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; devotion as dialogue, not obedience.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of the Counterfeit
chapters.summary: POV Sera. With the true covenant reforged, the stitched god loses its borrowed shape and unravels; those it healed keep their healing, but its marks fade. Sera's own sigil dissolves, and she finds she doesn't mourn it. Emotional beat: release, the strange lightness of no longer being claimed.

chapters.title: Terms of Service
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Ulyana, whole again, stands before her last faithful servant. She offers to restore his mark and their old bond. Xanthe refuses servitude and proposes partnership: gods who answer, mortals who may refuse. She laughs—first time in a decade—and agrees. Emotional beat: negotiation as intimacy; identity renegotiated.

chapters.title: A City That May Believe
chapters.summary: POV ensemble (Xanthe primary). Magic is decriminalized in Vask; Odile opens an honest charm-house; the widow becomes the first priestess of the new covenant. Xanthe keeps selling small charms, but now they work—and he turns away anyone who wants a god instead of a life. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on consent.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, coda. On the anniversary of the Silence, Xanthe lights a candle that stays lit. Ulyana's voice, warm and present, asks what he will pray for; he answers that he'll tell her in person, someday, but not yet. There is work to do, and time enough at last. Emotional beat: peace earned, story closed with an open door.
